claim: Kairos v4.4.0 is the latest stable release (published 2026-10-26); tag v4.4.0 points to commit 6f33334a6a6c88a4a38c0b7ec4df1ab0334b830d; previous stable v4.3.0 2026-09-08, v4.2.0 2026-08-18, v4.0.0 2026-02-27
Kairos is licensed Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file at the v4.4.0 tag)

Kairos is a monorepo since 2026: agent, immucore, kcrypt, sdk, kairos-init, installer and the p2p provider live in one tree and ship on one release tag; the historical repos (kairos-agent, immucore, kairos-sdk, kairos-init, provider-kairos, ...) are archived
Kairos was accepted to the CNCF on 2024-04-13 at the Sandbox maturity level
Five of six listed Kairos maintainers are affiliated with Spectro Cloud and one with Mirantis
The Kairos ADOPTERS file lists 5 organizations (3 Production with no dated status, 2 Proof of Concept dated 2026-04/05) and 2 individuals

Image build: images/Dockerfile takes any BASE_IMAGE and runs the kairos-init binary (bind-mounted from the kairos-init image) in two stages, install then init, with MODEL, TRUSTED_BOOT, KUBERNETES_DISTRO (k3s or k0s), KUBERNETES_VERSION and FIPS arguments; at the v4.4.0 tag the default kairos-init is still v0.17.3
kairos-init recognises Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL, Rocky, Alma, Oracle Linux, Fedora, Arch, Alpine, openSUSE Leap/Tumbleweed, SLES, SLE Micro Rancher and Hadron as base distributions

kairos-init's supported models at v4.4.0 are generic, rpi3, rpi4, nvidia-jetson-agx-orin, nvidia-jetson-orin-nx, nvidia-jetson-thor and nvidia-dgx-spark; there is no rpi5 and no Jetson Orin Nano model
For Debian on Raspberry Pi, kairos-init installs linux-image-arm64, firmware-linux-free and raspi-firmware for rpi3 and rpi4 only
Kairos docs: 'Model 5 is currently not supported because of how we use U-boot to boot the device'; supported Pi models are 3 and 4 (64-bit)
Kairos issue #2010 'Support for Raspberry Pi 5' is open (created 2023-11-17, last updated 2026-09-03)
Feature-set matrix: Debian 13 is built and tested in CI with CIS L1 and system extensions; Trusted Boot and FIPS on Debian 13 are 'not tested'; SELinux is not supported on Debian
Board matrix: Jetson AGX Orin and Orin NX are supported only on Ubuntu 22.04 (L4T r36.x); AGX Thor on Ubuntu 24.04 or Hadron (L4T r39.2); DGX Spark on Ubuntu 24.04; no board is documented on Debian
Jetson images are built by kairos-init --model with an Ubuntu base: AGX Orin and Orin NX on ubuntu:22.04 (r36.x), Thor on ubuntu:24.04 or Hadron (r39.2); the old Dockerfile.nvidia was removed
Orin NX install uses NVIDIA's Jetson Linux SDK flashing from a Linux host with a custom partition layout (OEM, COS_STATE, EFI, RECOVERY, optional PERSISTENT)

On Jetson Thor, Kairos keeps its own bootloader on the ESP: the QSPI script deliberately avoids the nvidia-l4t-bootloader postinst because it would replace BOOTAA64.efi with NVIDIA's L4TLauncher; it stages a UEFI capsule only when the image's firmware is newer and aborts on a downgrade
The Jetson QSPI firmware check runs in both after-install-chroot and after-upgrade-chroot, so an OS image upgrade also stages a newer boot-firmware capsule; a staging failure aborts the upgrade

Disk layout: a state partition holds active and passive images as loop-mounted .img files; a recovery partition holds a squashfs recovery image; OEM holds cloud-config; the persistent partition is mounted at /usr/local with bind mounts; kernel and initrd come from inside the image and are chain-loaded by GRUB

Upgrade code: if booted from active, the current active.img is renamed to passive.img (relabelled) and the new image becomes active; if booted from passive, only active is replaced so a working passive is never overwritten; recovery is upgraded separately with --recovery

GRUB boot assessment: after-upgrade sets enable_boot_assessment=yes; GRUB sets boot_assessment_tentative on first try and, if it sees it again, boots the fallback entry with upgrade_failure; the sentinels are cleared in the boot.before cloud-config stage on the active image

Docs: a boot counts as successful once the active image is mounted and cloud-init reaches boot.before; it does not wait for workloads or Kubernetes; automatic rollback is GRUB-only; manual rollback is 'kairos-agent bootentry --select fallback' for one boot
Trusted Boot (UKI) installs rename loader entries with a +3 boot-counting suffix and enable systemd-bless-boot, i.e. systemd-boot automatic boot assessment with 3 tries

Docs contradict code: boot_assessment.md says systemd automatic boot assessment is 'not yet implemented' for Trusted Boot and links issue #2864, but #2864 was closed 2024-11-27 and issue #5965 (open, 2026-11-05) reports the doc is wrong

Trusted Boot example doc: a UKI boot entry is marked good when multi-user.target is reached; 3 tries by default, then passive, then recovery; services can be tied into boot-complete.target to gate the assessment
Upgrade image signature check is opt-in on GRUB installs: DumpSource runs cosign verify only when config 'cosign: true' (bool, default false) with an optional cosign-key
Trusted Boot upgrades refuse a UKI whose Authenticode signer differs from the cert that verifies the currently booted UKI (same-signer rule), not merely any cert in the UEFI db
Release artifacts: ISO sha256 files and the binaries' checksums.txt are signed keylessly with cosign in CI (GitHub OIDC identity of the release workflow)

Kairos operator NodeOpUpgrade spec fields: nodeSelector, image, concurrency, stopOnFailure, upgradeRecovery, upgradeActive, force, uncordonOnFailure, excludePaths, resources; there is no schedule or maintenance-window field
Issue #6027 (open, 2026-11-09): automatic updates are 'not a feature of Kairos itself'; they must be built with the operator or a pipeline; depends on weekly releases (#5923)

Issue #6018: upgrading a 2023-installed UEFI+TPM node to v4.4.0 refreshed shim/GRUB on the ESP but left an old grub.cfg on COS_STATE; GRUB's tpm module then exhausted heap loading the 3 GiB image and active, fallback and recovery entries all failed to boot; fixed by PR #6028 (closed 2026-11-10)

Issue #4345: a Trusted Boot day-2 upgrade failed with kairos-agent v2.24.10 because the target image's loader entry used the newer 'uki' key ('no efi entry in .conf file'); reported from a CanvOS/Palette Edge build

Issue #4969 (open): once the OS and Kubernetes-as-extension upgrade independently, rollback can boot an OS/Kubernetes pairing the node never ran; nothing in the upgrade flow preserves a known-good pairing

v4.4.0 release notes: persisting /usr/libexec 'broke rollback across OS versions' and was dropped; immucore now fails the boot when persistent binds cannot mount (previously it booted silently without persistence, losing k3s state); CIS L1 hardening is on by default
Issue #5923 (open): Kairos 'tends to have minor 1-2 release per quarter'; proposal to move Kairos and Hadron to automatic weekly semver releases because of faster CVE discovery
No published per-release support period or end-of-life policy was found in the Kairos docs, SECURITY.md or community repo (searched 'supported version', 'end of life', 'backport', 'security fixes')
Bundles: install targets use container://, docker://, run:// or package:// schemes; run:// extracts an OCI image and executes its run.sh; no signature check exists in the bundle installer
System extensions live in /var/lib/kairos/extensions and are enabled per boot profile (active, passive, recovery, common) via symlinks into /run/extensions
systemd-sysext image policy: Trusted Boot requires signed extensions (root=signed+absent:usr=signed+absent); non-Trusted-Boot installs require dm-verity (verity+absent)
The agent resolves extensions by name from a published catalog (hadron-layers releases.json) and requires every resolved OCI reference to be digest-pinned (@sha256)
Issue #5032 (open): epic to move Kubernetes and the provider out of the 'standard' image into system extensions; contents and contract still undecided

The p2p provider in standard images is an agent plugin discovered under /system/providers and spoken to over a stdin/stdout event protocol; its mesh covers k3s only; other providers (provider-rke2, provider-k3s) are interchangeable
provider-kubeadm is archived; kubeadm support continues in provider-kubernetes, which tracks the three most recent upstream Kubernetes minors

Immucore: when a boot is blocked it shows a full-screen message and on systemd reboots after 90 seconds so boot assessment sees the failed boot; under Trusted Boot created partitions are TPM-PCR encrypted with no plaintext fallback

Install paths documented: interactive and automated ISO, manual, takeover from a rescue system, network boot (AuroraBoot), MAAS, WebUI, QR code shown at boot, p2p, raw images for SBCs, Trusted Boot installer
Hadron single-node with k3s: bare minimum 8 GB disk / 2 GB RAM (smoke tests only); practical minimum 16 GB disk / 4 GB RAM
Hadron is a Kairos-team distribution built from scratch on musl libc, systemd and an unpatched kernel
Commercial support for Kairos is sold by Spectro Cloud (announced 2025-08-08); the project states there are no commercial forks or gated features

Spectro Cloud Kairos support pricing: Community free; Basic $2k/year for 5 tickets; Production $10k/year for up to 50 nodes with 24x7 P1/P2; Production includes free Palette Edge for up to five edge clusters
Kairos AI integration is a documented LocalAI deployment on k3s via a community bundle; no MCP server or agent interface was found in the v4.4.0 tree or docs
No backup or restore feature for user or Kubernetes data is documented by Kairos (docs grep for 'backup' only finds CIS and kubeadm pages); persistence is the COS_PERSISTENT partition
